records.subject: Need to curb adult oriented and sexually explicit content in mobile applications meant for children.
records.SM_Text:
Smt Rajathi:

I seek to raise a matter that deserves due attention from the Government. During the proceedings of the World Wide Web Conference, a group of researchers from Monash University Australia presented their study on 25,000 mobile apps revealing the presence of sexual content ads in apps meant for children. These pornographic and age-inappropriate content should never be part of the limited or regulated digital exposure meant for our children.  We must ensure that our children are safe online from content risks involving children seeing inappropriate material. It is disturbing to note that sexually suggestive advertisements, nudity, dating services, and adult rated web-series are shown in educational and games apps used by children. There are game platforms that ask children to upload their photos, which the children readily upload without understanding the implications or seriousness. There are also reports on how Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) is being shared online on social media platforms. These developments raise serious concerns regarding child safety, privacy and compliance with applicable laws in India. Our children need to be safe. Recent data laid in the Parliament indicates that around 2.3 lakh POCSO cases remain pending in our courts highlighting how our children are regular victims, who need more stronger safeguards against every form of sexual exploitation, including exposure of sexually explicit content in digital environments. I urge the Government to look into it.

(ENDS)

Demand for integration of nutritious breakfast into the PM-POSHAN Scheme.
records.SM_Text:
Smt. Rajathi: I bring attention of the Government to a critical recommendation of integrating the provision of a nutritious breakfast in addition to the midday meal in government schools. Research consistently shows that the morning hours are the most productive for learning. However, a significant portion of our students from economically marginalized backgrounds arrive at school on an empty stomach, which severely disturbs their concentration and academic outcomes.  While States like Tamil Nadu have successfully launched the Chief Minister?s Breakfast Scheme, benefitting lakhs and lakhs of students which shows a marked improvement in attendance and health, many other States are unable to scale such initiatives due to financial constraints. In view of the fact that India still faces high rates of child wasting and stunting, this is would be a necessary investment in our human capital. I, therefore, urge the Government to formally include breakfast in the Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM-POSHAN) scheme, provide a dedicated budget for this expansion to support States, upgrade kitchen infrastructure in government schools to ensure the safe and hygienic preparation of two meals per day. School meals twice a day would ensure hunger doesnt stop children from learning and staying healthy.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand for comprehensive reforms in juvenile homes under the Juvenile Justice Act.
records.SM_Text:
Smt. Rajathi: I draw attention of the Government over alarming conditions in the juvenile homes, where there is inadequate monitoring, nutrition, education and safety that continue to expose children to severe vulnerabilities. This is evident from repeated news on children being beaten to death in these institutes and severe overcrowding. Juvenile homes are governed by the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015- under which each district is required to have an observation home for children facing trial before the Juvenile Justice Board. As per the latest National Crime Record Bureau report (2023 data), juvenile crime in India is 7.1 per lakh children, 31,365 cases registered. These numbers are more worrying when seen with the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) inspections that have highlighted overcrowding, poor resources, poor food quality, untrained staff and lack of psychological support in several childcare institutions. The Juvenile Justice system is the product of a system built supposedly to protect and rehabilitate children, but in reality it functions more as a punitive institution of neglect. If we expect these children to reintegrate into society with dignity, I urge the Government to strengthen monitoring mechanisms, upgrade nutrition and education standards, ensure accountability in staff recruitment and create meaningful livelihood opportunities so that our juvenile homes become places of protection and hope, not fear.

(ENDS)
